sm: President Trump wraps up his whirlwind Asia trip and reassures Americans that they are safe from cyber attacks by state actors. He says anyone who did that to the country would know the repercussions. The hosts, John Bickley and Georgia Howe, introduce the Friday, November 20th edition. They preview a Senate effort led by one senator to expose online gaming platforms that leave children vulnerable, noting that one platform has 150 million daily users and has been called a haven for sex predators. They also preview a conversation with a gaming expert about Grand Theft Auto 6, which is setting record sales.

Air Force One returned to Washington late Thursday night after President Trump's three-day Asia trip. Cabot Phillips reports that the trip began in the Philippines with announcements on an Alaska pipeline step and more than 17 billion dollars in deals. The main event was the first trilateral meeting of Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, lasting about an hour and a half. Trump said the three nuclear powers were uniquely positioned to reduce nuclear weapons and keep Iran from getting one. They also discussed the wars in Iran and Ukraine and issued an identical joint declaration toward peace, covering UN reform, petroleum supplies, state immunities and a follow-up dialogue on nuclear risks. Washington skeptics say words on paper differ from actions. On the domestic outages, Trump called the reaction an overreaction and said they are individual events, while officials told Congress they are unrelated and not nefarious. Prepper companies report sales up 400 to 500 percent. Chase said hackers hit outside vendors, exposing names and email addresses, in an attack unconnected to Monday's outages. A new ransomware group claimed the data, gave Chase 48 hours to pay or face a leak tied to more than 16,000 customers, and also targeted Visa and Expedia.

A Senate hearing this week heard victim testimony about child exploitation on the gaming platform Roblox. Senator Josh Hawley, who led it, says he still thinks the recent string of outages is no coincidence, noting he and other senators have not been properly briefed. He describes Roblox as one of the largest gaming platforms, with 75 percent of American children aged 9 to 12 on it, a 33 billion dollar value and 150 million daily users. He says it is a haven for sex predators. His central concern is forced arbitration, which stops child victims from going to court, presenting evidence or facing a jury, and he wants it banned for child victims of online sex crimes. He cites hundreds of documented cases and says there are probably thousands more. He recounts a survivor who was abused at 11, became a Marine, and told no one for decades. Hawley says the government should open the courthouse doors, and calls Roblox's selfie-based age checks a joke.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is released after a 13-year wait, with pre-order sales estimated near 1.65 billion dollars. A pastor is heard objecting to constant exposure to violence. Gaming journalist Colin Moriarty, who co-hosts the Sacred Symbols podcast, explains that GTA is an open-world action game where players do whatever they like. He says it is a rare unifying moment in a fractured industry, with satire, soundtracks and a new Vice City setting based on Miami. At 80 dollars, or nearly 100 for the premium edition, and an estimated 1.5 billion dollar development cost, he says it reflects an industry expected to earn about 220 billion dollars this year. He says violence has always been central but is meant as lampooning, and that the sexual content is overt but tied to the story. He respects people who choose not to play, notes it is protected speech, and says age limits apply to purchases.
